stem:
Asha throws a ball straight up. The ball slows, stops briefly, then falls and speeds up.

Which claim correctly explains the motion?

options.text: Earth pulls the ball toward itself the whole time, so the ball slows going up and speeds up coming down.
The ball carries an upward force from the throw until that force runs out; Earth pulls only after the ball starts falling.
An object thrown upward speeds up until it leaves Earth.
Earth pushes the ball upward while the ball rises.

teacher.key_rationale: Gravitational attraction between Earth and the ball acts throughout, slowing the rise and speeding the fall. Saying Earth pulls only on the way down drops continuous attraction. Speeding up while leaving Earth reverses the slowing on the way up. An upward push from Earth swaps attraction for a push.
